clue.text: Di looks so chic, the bird !

annotationWithheld.why: Di looks so chic, the bird! (6): the bird DIPPER with its I changed to A gives chic DAPPER, but no clue word signals the letter change; 'Di looks so' reads as garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Di looks so chic, the bird !

clue.text: All-red trunk route.

parts.note: the main vessel of the body carrying only bright oxygenated blood, a trunk line in the anatomical sense

explanation.surface: A railway or road line painted red on the map from end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest artery leaves the heart as the body's main trunk, carrying oxygen-rich red blood.

clue.text: One cop's hat -I-reshape to fit nut

indicators.note: to reshape something is to give it a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written, with its S
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A policeman squashes his helmet to make it fit over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshape' rearranges I plus COPS, HAT and I into the green nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistachio is a green-kernelled nut from a Middle Eastern tree.

clue.text: Sharp girl's'uncouth fellow

definitions.note: the possessive points to the husband belonging to Becky Sharp, so it stands for a man's name

parts.note: uncouth means raw, rough and unpolished
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: A clever young woman's boyfriend has no manners.
explanation.walkthrough: Becky Sharp, heroine of Thackeray's Vanity Fair, marries Rawdon Crawley, so 'Sharp girl's' means her man. 'Sharp' looks like an adjective for a clever girl.
explanation.definitionFit: In Vanity Fair, Becky Sharp's husband is the soldier Rawdon Crawley.

clue.text: Strike action in: the: shoeshine trade

definitions.meaning: unions refusing to handle goods or work during a dispute
polish used on boots by shoeblacks

explanation.surface: Shoe polishers walk out in an industrial dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Unions boycotting goods is called blacking them, and blacking was also the old name for boot polish.

clue.text: Scene, of many a hanging after a frame-up.

definitions.text: Scene, of many a hanging after a frame-up.

parts.words: Scene, of many a hanging after a frame-up.
parts.note: a gallery where pictures are framed and then hung on the walls, not an execution of a man wrongly accused

explanation.surface: A gallows where innocent men are executed after being framed.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House in London's Piccadilly is home of the Royal Academy, whose Summer Exhibition hangs hundreds of framed paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Academy's building in Piccadilly hosts the Summer Exhibition, where framed paintings are hung.

clue.text: Bunks, primarily seamen's

parts.note: to do a bunk is to run away, and the word for it begins with AB'S, the seamen's

explanation.surface: Beds on board are mostly for the sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunks' looks like ship's beds but is the verb, doing a bunk. The opening letters are able seamen's.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a bunk means running off secretly, which is what deserters and fugitives do.

clue.text: Uncapsizable canoe ?

indicators.note: a craft that cannot be turned over reads the same when its letters are turned round

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A small boat that cannot overturn.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a palindrome, so turning it upside down (end to end) changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit kayak is a covered canoe paddled with a double blade.

clue.text: Town where F.D.R.'s policy could have been effected?

definitions.text: Town where F.D.R.'s policy could have been effected?

parts.words: Town where F.D.R.'s policy could have been effected?
parts.note: Roosevelt's policy was the New Deal, and a deal is made in the card game named after a Suffolk racing town

explanation.surface: Wondering which town could have put Roosevelt's economic plan into action.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is a Suffolk horse-racing town and also a card game, where a new deal is dealt.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is the Suffolk home of British flat racing, and shares its name with a card game.

clue.text: Puzzling games' of Snap?

definitions.meaning: puzzles solved from clues on a grid
an irritable retort is a sharp exchange of angry remarks

explanation.surface: A card game of Snap seems a puzzling pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzles with clues and grids are one sense; angry or irritable remarks such as a snap are the other.

clue.text: You turn south-west at the copse

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

indicators.note: turning a short abbreviation round means the compass letters are read backwards

parts.note: SW is the compass abbreviation for south-west

explanation.surface: Directions telling someone to go left by a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is the reversal signal for the compass pair; 'You' as YE is the archaic pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A clump of evergreen trees of one kind can form a small wood or copse.

clue.text: Dishy old dandy

definitions.meaning: read as being a dish of food, here pasta
an 18th-century fop who affected continental fashions

explanation.surface: A good-looking elderly gentleman who dresses well.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a pasta dish, and in the 1700s a foppish young man returned from the Grand Tour was given the same name.

clue.text: Town has the wherewithal to smoke its pig

parts.note: oak wood chips are burnt to cure and smoke meat
ham is cured meat from a pig's leg

explanation.surface: A town boasting it has what it takes to cure its bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: Oakham is the county town of Rutland, England's smallest county.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakham is the county town of Rutland in the English Midlands.

clue.text: King looked at by a long-haired cat?

definitions.text: looked at by a long-haired cat?
definitions.meaning: the proverb says a cat may look at a king, and the long-haired cat is a Persian, so a Persian monarch

explanation.surface: A monarch is stared at by a fluffy cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a cat may look at a king' lies behind it; a Persian is a long-haired breed of cat, and the ruler of Persia was the shah.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the old ruler of Persia (Iran) was the Persian word for king.

clue.text: Two such annuals are the .. making of a novelist

definitions.text: Two such annuals are the .. making of a novelist

parts.words: Two such annuals are the .. making of a novelist
parts.note: two halves of the novelist Thomas's surname make the whole of it, and annuals of this type need some frost protection

explanation.surface: A writer is shaped by reading two yearbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: Annuals here are garden plants; two halves of HARDY make Thomas Hardy, the novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that survive outdoors but need shelter from frost when young are described this way by gardeners.

clue.text: Travelling menagerie reaches borders of Kansas-Gosh!

parts.note: to gad is to travel about restlessly
a menagerie is a collection of wild animals, a zoo

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters, here of Kansas

explanation.surface: A touring animal show arrives in a US state, to surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders of' takes the first and last letters of Kansas, K and S.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic oath of surprise, like 'Gosh!', from 'God's hooks'.

clue.text: Vital function of some tents

parts.note: hospital tents placed over patients feed them a life-giving gas

explanation.surface: The essential purpose of camping shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: The tents are oxygen tents in hospitals, which enrich a patient's air.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplying the blood or air with life-giving gas is what a hospital oxygen tent does.

clue.text: Property pincher ?

parts.note: real estate is land
a crab has pinching claws

explanation.surface: A thief who steals real estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pincher' looks like a thief, but it is a creature with claws.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab that lives mostly on land in the tropics, with nipping claws.

clue.text: Mangold land

parts.note: split as man, gold, land: the golden country that men sought, not a field of beets

explanation.surface: A field where mangold beet is grown.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangold is a beet grown as fodder; split, the words suggest the fabled golden land of South America that conquistadors hunted.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled city of gold sought by Spanish explorers in South America.

clue.text: Was there ever one, let alone still one in existence?

definitions.text: Was there ever one, let alone still one in existence?

parts.note: still in the sense of yet, so far
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Doubting whether such a creature ever existed, let alone survives today.
explanation.walkthrough: The Himalayan abominable snowman may never have existed at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a creature whose existence is doubted.

clue.text: Scots: grey mare's habiliments

parts.note: the Scottish word for trousers, worn by the grey mare, the wife who rules her husband

explanation.surface: Gear for a grey horse of the Scots Greys cavalry regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The grey mare is the better horse' says the wife wears the trousers; the Scots Greys were a cavalry regiment, a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeks is the Scots form of breeches, the trousers a domineering wife is said to wear.

clue.text: Keats's Grecian urn was this with some who' did and were

definitions.text: Keats's Grecian urn was this with some who' did and were

parts.words: Keats's Grecian urn was this with some who' did and were
parts.note: the urn is engraved with figures, some pursuing and some pursued, so one word means both

explanation.surface: Musing on the decoration of the urn in Keats's ode.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's ode asks 'What mad pursuit?' of the figures; the urn was engraved, and some figures did the pursuing and some were pursued.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal or pottery engraved with designs is described this way, as are those pursued.

clue.text: A form of outer covering

definitions.meaning: a class in some English public schools between the lower and upper forms
the hard casing of an egg, nut or mollusc

explanation.surface: Describing a kind of external wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: In some British public schools the Shell is a form, a year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard outside case is one sense; a school class at some English public schools is the other.

clue.text: Lady gardener to whom Napoleon III owed his life

definitions.meaning: a woman's name echoing the Latin for 'of the garden'

definitions.text: to whom Napoleon III owed his life
definitions.meaning: the Queen of Holland who was the mother of the French emperor

explanation.surface: A woman who tended plants once saved an emperor's life.
explanation.walkthrough: Hortense de Beauharnais was Napoleon III's mother, so he owed her his life by birth, not rescue; Latin 'hortensis' means of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin root means of the garden, and Hortense de Beauharnais was the emperor's mother.

clue.text: Base member, crooked as close

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of shape, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A lowly gang member, as bent as they come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges the letters of CLOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth supporting a column or statue is an architectural base element.

clue.text: Like. Yeats's lake island house?

parts.note: Yeats's lake isle was ..., read as 'inn is' plus a word meaning without charge

explanation.surface: Asking what the poet's cottage on the lake was like.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeats's poem is 'The Lake Isle of Innisfree'; split as 'Inn is free', the house on it is without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Costing nothing, as the split of the poem's island name suggests of its inn.

clue.text: The way to go: is left and right, Tommy

definitions.text: The way to go: is left and right, Tommy

parts.note: a route is the way to go
the drill call 'left, right' marks the steps of a march

explanation.surface: Advice to a soldier on which way to walk.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is a British private soldier, from Tommy Atkins; a route march is a long training march.
explanation.definitionFit: A long training walk for soldiers, timed by the call of left, right.

clue.text: The one utter effort of sly Bella perhaps.

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters may be one possible arrangement among others, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Sly Bella made only a single attempt at saying anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SLY and BELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of speech produced in one push of breath counts as a single utterance.

clue.text: So could some cash eke limited means of a levanter

indicators.note: some of the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Thinking some money could stretch a runaway debtor's limited resources.
explanation.walkthrough: A levanter is someone from the Levant (and also a welsher who runs off); the shekel is Israel's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The shekel is the money of ancient and modern Israel in the Levant.
